purpose: This medication is used to treat the symptoms of Parkinson's disease, such as tremors, stiffness, and slow movement. It helps make it easier to move and do everyday activities. It combines three medicines that work together to give you better, longer-lasting relief than some other Parkinson's medicines.
how_it_works: Levodopa is converted into dopamine in your brain, which is the chemical that helps control your movement. Carbidopa helps more levodopa reach your brain and reduces side effects like nausea. Entacapone helps levodopa last longer in your body so the effects are more steady throughout the day.
common_side_effects: You may notice nausea, dizziness, or feeling lightheaded, especially when standing up. Some people experience uncontrolled movements (called dyskinesias), drowsiness, or confusion. Your urine, sweat, or saliva may turn a harmless brownish-orange color. Diarrhea can also happen, especially when you first start the medicine.
warnings: Do not stop taking this medicine suddenly without talking to your doctor, as this can cause serious problems. Tell your doctor if you notice unusual urges like gambling or compulsive behaviors. This medicine can cause low blood pressure when standing, so rise slowly from sitting or lying down. Let your doctor know about all your other medicines, especially MAO inhibitors, as dangerous interactions can occur. If you have liver problems or a history of melanoma, talk to your doctor before taking this medication.
typical_dosing: This medicine is usually taken by mouth 3 to 8 times a day, depending on your individual needs. It comes in different strengths, and your doctor will choose the right one for you. Take it at evenly spaced times and try to take it with or without food consistently. Do not crush or break the tablets — swallow them whole.
